account:
It is six in the morning on day 1, and I have just woken at home. Today's known appointments are office at eight, grain inspection at the east-bank mill at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, and home at nineteen. I should read the appointment book this morning to confirm them.

I still suspect there is activity in town I do not understand, but have little verified evidence. The neighbour reported unexplained lights at the bakery and seeing the baker give freight bread after a discussion about the market. The baker denied installing new lights and said they declined an unsolicited repair or lighting offer from the builder. I have not established who installed any lights, when, or whether they indicate anything unusual. I asked the builder for firsthand information yesterday but could not make out the reply.

There is also a rumour concerning the crossing, traced to Townsfolk 02 and 22, without concrete details. Freight denied knowing about it. It would be wrong to treat that rumour as an established event or connect it to the bakery without evidence.

Freight gave the secretary a written book and offered deliveries at two emeralds per load. The secretary says no municipal work has been authorized and the offer is filed. Freight subsequently asked about authorization and possible consignments, saying they would be available at the warehouse and ferry. This could simply be an effort to obtain delivery business; the bread transfer could likewise be ordinary trade. I do not yet know of a secret gathering or coordinated plan. My best course is to keep my appointments and seek specific firsthand observations, particularly from the builder and the two sources of the crossing rumour, without spreading unsupported suspicions.
